brief: #149 built --additions: a quota on the three surfaces a worker appends to and every later iteration re-reads (one ledger entry <= 1.8 KB, at most one inventory line and one cue, 250 B each). run-loop.sh never calls it - it only runs the pre-iteration --terse - so the quota binds only if a worker chooses to obey SKILL.md. That is a gate that exists at a rate of zero, which is a law in this repo, and the cost is measurable: the read budget has opened OVER on roughly thirty consecutive worker iterations and been reset by six manager passes. Wire it. After the worker's commit, run --additions --since HEAD~1 and surface a non-zero exit in the run log the way the other post-iteration gates are surfaced.
successLooksLike: A staged over-quota tree makes the runner report the named offender and which surface it was on; a clean iteration is silent; HEAD passes with exit 0.
avoid: Do not make it revert or block the commit - a memory-quota breach is a REPORT, not a revert, and a runner that reverts good work over a 260 B cue is worse than the drift. Do not re-open the quota's numbers; #149 set them and five open cues and seven inventory lines pre-date the cap, so grandfather what exists and bind only what an iteration ADDS. Keep it small: this is a 15-minute brief, not a harness rewrite.
